chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Do not pick your teeth with a twig of basil, nor with a shoot of pomegranate, for these two agitate the vein of leprosy.
ai.seo_question: Why should one avoid using basil or pomegranate twigs for teeth cleaning according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides specific medical wisdom regarding oral hygiene, cautioning against using basil or pomegranate twigs as toothpicks because they are believed to aggravate the 'vein of leprosy' (irq al-jutham). This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating practical health advice with spiritual and physical well-being, emphasizing preventive care in daily Sunnah practices.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Do not pick teeth with a stem of basil, nor with a stem of the pomegranate, for these two agitate the vein of leprosy’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If one uses reeds as toothpicks none of his wishes can come true for six days.’”
